artifacts.synopsis: A church member challenged Heritage Presbytery's ruling that the BCO neither expressly nor implicitly requires a congregation to approve changes in a pastor's call, and that it does not require the session to publicize budget details. The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. The complaint was not sustained; seven commissioners dissented, arguing congregational approval follows by good and necessary consequence.

artifacts.synopsis: A member challenged Presbytery’s approval of a congregational motion supplementing an assistant-pastor fund, alleging that Session had ceded its budget authority. The SJC denied both issues. The motion addressed a special circumstance, not approval of the budget, and left the salary figure to the elders and deacons; Session had already approved the budget and retained control of church funds. The ruling was confined to the congregation’s particular circumstances and did not approve congregational budget adoption.

artifacts.title: Session authority over church budget versus congregational call terms

matches.evidence: The CCB answered yes: under BCO 12-5.b, the session's duty to approve the budget supersedes the congregation's authority to set pastoral call terms in any fiscal year.

artifacts.title: Session authority to approve ministerial severance packages

matches.evidence: CCB advised that sessions may approve severance packages for ministers without congregational approval, as these are budgetary matters under BCO 12-5b.

artifacts.title: Session's right to access congregation's financial and attendance records

matches.evidence: CCB advised that the session and diaconate have a right to access financial and attendance records as needed, limited only by prudence and protection of reputation.
